questions.question: Which three aspects are used to organize cybersickness evaluation strategies?
options: User, developer, and system
Input, latency, and output
Detection, prediction, and mitigation
Input, process, and output
questions.explanation: Cybersickness evaluation strategies can be organized into input, process, and output.

questions.question: What do interpretable machine learning models offer in cybersickness evaluation?
options: Guaranteed higher accuracy than black-box models
Less flexibility in customization and model use
More precise details about input-output relationships
A hidden process that cannot be explained
questions.explanation: Interpretable models are similar to transparent models and provide precise details about the relationships between input and output.

questions.question: What trade-off is generally associated with black-box models in cybersickness evaluation?
options: Higher transparency with larger data and processing power needs
Higher prediction accuracy with larger data and processing power needs
Greater interpretability with less predictive performance
Lower prediction accuracy with smaller data and processing power needs
questions.explanation: Black-box models generally provide higher prediction accuracy than transparent and interpretable models, but require large amounts of data and processing power.

questions.question: What do hybrid models in machine learning evaluation of cybersickness aim to provide?
options: Only transparency with low predictive performance
High accuracy and transparency in their decision-making
Only high accuracy with hidden decision-making
Only accuracy from a single black-box model
questions.explanation: Hybrid models combine different machine learning models to provide high accuracy and transparency, combining strengths of transparent and black-box models.

questions.question: In cybersickness evaluation, what distinguishes detection from prediction?
options: Detection uses input generated after the experience; prediction uses input generated before it.
Detection uses input generated during the experience; prediction uses input generated after it.
Detection uses input generated after the experience; prediction uses input generated during it.
Detection uses input generated before the experience; prediction uses input generated after it.
questions.explanation: Detection determines whether cybersickness has occurred using input generated after the experience, while prediction determines whether it will occur before the experience.

questions.question: Why is prediction valuable in cybersickness evaluation?
options: It can enable mitigation measures after cybersickness occurs.
It can enable mitigation measures before cybersickness occurs.
It can replace self-report scores for assessing severity.
It can confirm whether cybersickness has already occurred.
questions.explanation: Prediction is important because it can allow mitigation before cybersickness occurs, even though most cybersickness evaluation work focuses on detection.

questions.question: What kinds of outputs can machine-learning-based cybersickness evaluation produce?
options: Classification labels or a numerical sickness score.
Only a numerical sickness score from a regression model.
Physiological signals or video features.
Only classification labels, such as sickness or no sickness.
questions.explanation: Machine-learning-based cybersickness evaluation can produce either classification labels or a numerical sickness score.

questions.question: In machine-learning-based cybersickness evaluation, how do classification labels differ from a sickness score?
options: Labels are generally regression outputs; scores are generally classification outputs.
Scores indicate likelihood or severity; labels quantify severity and are generally regression outputs.
Labels can only be binary; scores can be low, moderate, or acute.
Labels indicate likelihood or severity; scores quantify severity and are generally regression outputs.
questions.explanation: Classification labels indicate the likelihood or severity of cybersickness, while a sickness score quantifies the severity of the experience and is generally produced by a regression model.

questions.question: Why is cybersickness mitigation usually framed as reducing or lessening cybersickness rather than complete prevention?
options: Because mitigation only requires measures from the user's perspective
Because complete prevention is generally possible with developer-side measures
Because complete prevention is generally not possible
Because cybersickness is always caused by improper user behavior
questions.explanation: Complete prevention of cybersickness is generally not possible, so mitigation uses measures to reduce, eliminate, or lessen its impact.

questions.question: What trade-off is involved in mitigating cybersickness?
options: Reducing sickness may strengthen presence and user experience
Preserving presence may completely eliminate cybersickness
Reducing sickness may compromise presence and user experience
Restricting field of view can improve presence and visual-task performance
questions.explanation: Mitigation strategies can affect presence or the user's ability to perceive the virtual world, and presence affects user experience.

questions.question: Why must cybersickness mitigation consider both developer and user perspectives?
options: Because only the developer's perspective is needed to prevent cybersickness
Because a good developer solution may fail if the user uses it improperly
Because a good developer solution always succeeds even if the user uses it improperly
Because only the user's perspective is needed to prevent cybersickness
questions.explanation: Even a good developer solution may fail to prevent cybersickness if the user does not use the system properly or as expected.

questions.question: Why can field-of-view adjustment mitigate the onset or severity of cybersickness?
options: It maintains a stationary virtual nose in front of the user
It reduces peripheral optical flow
It increases the amount of visible virtual environment
It keeps the ground plane visible during movement
questions.explanation: Field-of-view adjustment can mitigate the onset or severity of cybersickness because restricting the field of view reduces peripheral optical flow.

questions.question: Which cybersickness-mitigation technique is described as an adaptive restrictor that obscures peripheral regions with higher optical flow during virtual locomotion?
options: An asymmetric mask
A symmetric mask
A rest frame
A dynamic visual blur
questions.explanation: An asymmetric mask is considered an adaptive restrictor because it obscures peripheral regions with higher optical flow while leaving regions with lower optical flow visible.

questions.question: What are the two types of dynamic visual blur described for reducing cybersickness?
options: Depth-of-field blur and peripheral blur
Depth-of-field blur and rest frames
Peripheral blur and optical-flow mixing
Depth-of-field blur and geometrical simplification
questions.explanation: Dynamic visual blur has two types: depth-of-field blur, which uses depth cues in human vision, and peripheral blur, also called dynamic non-salient region blurring.

questions.question: What are rest frames attached to the head reference frame called?
options: Virtual nose displays
Independent visual backgrounds
Peripheral visual backgrounds
Fixed visual backgrounds
questions.explanation: Rest frames attached to the head reference frame are known as independent visual backgrounds, with examples including clouds, grids, and a virtual nose.

questions.question: How does the Phantom legs hardware alteration reduce cybersickness?
options: It uses short bursts of rotational acceleration matching visual forward acceleration
It applies alternating haptic cues synchronized to the user's footsteps
It uses two small vibration motors behind the ears during walking
It expands the HMD periphery with a colorful LED matrix
questions.explanation: Phantom legs applies alternating haptic cues synchronized to users' footsteps using additional hardware, and was found to reduce cybersickness to a great extent.

questions.question: Why are user-side countermeasures needed to reduce the effects of cybersickness?
options: Because susceptibility to cybersickness is subjective and varies between users.
Because susceptibility to cybersickness is identical for all users
Because a one-size-fits-all developer-side approach is sufficient
Because users cannot add their own countermeasures
questions.explanation: Cybersickness is subjective, and individual susceptibility varies, so developer-side interventions alone may not be enough.

questions.question: What user-side exposure practice can reduce the risk of cybersickness?
options: Take a single long session instead of shorter sessions
Avoid continuous or long-duration exposure to a virtual environment.
Use one fixed exposure duration for all users
Increase exposure time until symptoms disappear
questions.explanation: Users may be advised to avoid continuous or long-duration virtual environment exposure, because longer exposure is risky and the safe duration can vary.

questions.question: How can users attempt habituation to a virtual environment?
options: Continue longer-duration exposures while cybersickness symptoms remain
Use repeated long-duration exposures first, then shorter-duration exposures after symptoms appear
Use repeated short-duration exposures until symptoms appear, then repeated longer-duration exposures after full recovery.
Use only short-duration exposures and stop as soon as symptoms appear
questions.explanation: The two-stage approach starts with repeated short exposures until symptoms appear, then moves to longer exposures after full recovery.

questions.question: What can slow diaphragmatic or controlled breathing help with regarding cybersickness?
options: Delay onset, increase severity, and increase the possibility of cybersickness
Increase onset speed, reduce severity, and reduce the possibility of cybersickness
Delay onset, reduce severity, and largely reduce the possibility of cybersickness.
Delay onset, reduce severity, and guarantee complete prevention of cybersickness
questions.explanation: Controlled breathing can delay the onset, reduce the severity, and largely reduce the possibility of cybersickness.

questions.question: Which user-side strategies can calm or soothe the mind and reduce cybersickness?
options: Playing unpleasant background music and avoiding external air flow
Playing pleasant background music and using continuous virtual exposure
Playing pleasant background music and ensuring adequate external air flow.
Ensuring adequate external air flow and increasing virtual session length
questions.explanation: Pleasant background music and adequate external air flow are user-side strategies that can calm or soothe the mind and reduce cybersickness.

questions.question: Why might a developer of a machine-learning cybersickness evaluator need to weigh prediction accuracy against understandability when comparing transparent, interpretable, and black-box models?
questions.reference_answer: Transparent models provide clear insight into the decision-making process, and interpretable models are similar, offering more flexibility in customization and more precise details about the relationship between input and output. Black-box models cannot easily be understood or explained because they take an input and produce an output without revealing how or why that output is generated. Black-box models generally provide higher prediction accuracy than transparent and interpretable models, but they require large amounts of data and processing power.

questions.question: How does prediction differ from detection in cybersickness evaluation, and why can prediction still support mitigation even though most evaluation work focuses on detection?
questions.reference_answer: Detection uses input generated after the experience to determine whether cybersickness has occurred, whereas prediction occurs before the experience to determine whether it will occur. Most cybersickness evaluation focuses on detection, but prediction is important because it can enable mitigation measures before cybersickness occurs. Because complete prevention is generally not possible, mitigation uses measures to reduce or eliminate cybersickness or at least lessen its impact.

questions.question: Why can a field-of-view adjustment reduce cybersickness while also creating a cost for user experience?
questions.reference_answer: Field of view is the amount of virtual environment visible at any moment, and adjusting it can mitigate cybersickness because restricting the field of view reduces peripheral optical flow. However, this restriction can reduce presence or sense of presence and impair performance in visual tasks. Since mitigation strategies often affect presence, and presence affects user experience, field-of-view adjustment can improve comfort while degrading user experience.

questions.question: How do hybrid cybersickness-evaluation models try to balance the higher accuracy of black-box models with the transparency of transparent or interpretable models?
questions.reference_answer: Black-box models generally provide higher prediction accuracy than transparent and interpretable models, but they require large amounts of data and processing power. Hybrid models are combinations of different machine learning models designed to provide high accuracy and transparency in their decision-making process. They can combine the strengths of transparent and black-box models by providing good predictive accuracy and some interpretability, which is useful in application domains where both high accuracy and transparency are essential.
